text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- 1996 net profit of chemicals concern DSM lower than expected. (p1)
- Offshore appliances and dredger maker IHC Caland sees profit growth slowing down. (p1)
- New Dutch cartel authority should force Ahold to sell its 73 pct stake in rival Schuitema, says small business association MKB. (p1)
- Dutch businesses consider governments' minimum wage plan to be just a political game. (p1)
- Automation group Baan Company boosts Q4 net to $ 15.8 million; Baan forecasts profit growth to accelerate. (p3)
- Staff of steelmaker Hoogovens to hold a demonstration today against threatening jobs loss. (p3)
- Engineering bureau DHV books seven million guilders 1996 net against 17 million guilders loss in 1995. (p3)
- Central bank DNB's warning of financial services group Fortis' unit NMKN seems to be unjust. (p9)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Minister for housing and regional development and environment as yet against building a second airport. (p1)
- Small businesses use legal tricks to fire sick staff, according to a lawyer. (p1)
- Number of starting entrepreneurs in the Netherlands is growing fast. (p2)
- Majority of MPs wants filling station supermarkets to remain small. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dog owners in Amsterdam and The Hague may face fines for dog dirt in the street of up to 2,000 guilders. (p1)
- Violent crimes committed by youth rise explosively compared to five years ago. (p1)
- Steelconcern Hoogovens demands action from Belgium's steel company Boel, if joint venture is to go through. (p21)
- Dutch regional transport group VSN considers traffic minister's plan for competition in 2000 too fast. (p23)
TROUW
- Labelling of soy products unreliable as consumer cannot be sure there really is no genetically manipulated soy in a product -- research. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Export of beef to Germany collapses after recent BSE scare. (p10)
- Tension at harbour concern HES' unit EBS mounts as banks stop money supply on Saturday. (p10)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
